analytical_question: How far has ambient clinical scribing diffused and when should this safety-net network pilot it?
general_et_finding: Ambient AI scribing is entering the early majority because 81% of surveyed physicians use AI and Vanderbilt rapidly expanded ambient scribing.
application_finding: For outpatient primary-care note drafting, relative advantage is reduced documentation burden; compatibility depends on EHR integration; complexity is moderate; trialability is high through a pilot; observability is high through note-time metrics.
organization_specific_finding: A conservative safety-net network should follow peers and wait until ambient scribing is more established before considering a pilot.

evidence.claim: 81% of surveyed physicians reported any awareness or use of AI
evidence.notes: This is broad AI, not ambient-scribe use.

evidence.claim: 20.1% of visit notes at one system used ambient scribing by March 31, 2025

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No representative ambient-scribe adoption denominator is available.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in early-majority stage; local peer data remain limited.
risk_governance_implication: Keep clinician sign-off and assess privacy.
recommendation_management_implication: Wait for more peer evidence before beginning a pilot.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Local EHR integration and privacy review
